added_models.model: Human 19-28z CAR T cells in SCID-beige mice bearing intraperitoneal Raji tumours (CRS model)

safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use (epub 28 May 2018).
safety.note: Built after clinical CRS was known, to reproduce it with the class's own 19-28z CAR.
safety.quote: Here we report a murine model of CRS that develops within 2-3 d of CAR T cell infusion and that is potentially lethal and responsive to IL-6 receptor blockade.

safety.magnitude_basis: serum cytokine profile (18 of 19 clinically reported cytokines) and IL-6R-blockade response
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6410714); citation markers dropped from quote.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: patient CRS (Brentjens 2013, Davila 2014) preceded the model. Neurotoxicity absent in mice, so called partial rather than a full reproduction.
safety.note: Reproduced clinical CRS cytokines and tocilizumab-like rescue, but showed no neurotoxicity, which patients had.
safety.quote: Remarkably, the serum cytokine profile elicited in these mice was highly similar to that reported in clinical studies

added_models.model: CD19- or CD44v6-CAR T cells in HSPC-humanized NSG-SGM3 mice with high ALL-CM leukemia burden (CRS/neurotoxicity model)

safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use (epub 28 May 2018).
safety.note: Humanized-mouse model built after clinical CRS and neurotoxicity were known, to reproduce both.
safety.quote: Herein, we describe a mouse model recapitulating key features of CRS and neurotoxicity.

safety.magnitude_basis: fever, IL-6 rise and delayed lethal neurotoxicity vs clinical CAR T toxicity
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only (paywalled); CD19 and CD44v6 CARs both used per ACIR digest, not verified in full text.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction; not a member product, product_in_model false. CD44v6-CAR arms are a sibling target and are not the basis of the call.
safety.note: Reproduced burden-dependent CRS with IL-6 and delayed meningeal neurotoxicity seen in CAR T patients.
safety.quote: In humanized mice with high leukemia burden, CAR T cell-mediated clearance of cancer triggered high fever and elevated IL-6 levels, which are hallmarks of CRS.

added_models.model: Conventional vs IL-6-shRNA (ssCART-19) CD19 CAR T cells in NOD/SCID/gamma-c-null mice bearing luciferase Raji cells

safety.confidence_note: Opening entry at first use (Research Square preprint Mar 2020; journal 8 Jun 2020).
safety.note: ssCART-19 (IL-6 shRNA CD19 CAR) vs conventional CART-19 in NSG mice bearing Raji: lower serum IL-6, same antitumour effect, predicting less severe CRS.
safety.short: Mouse: IL-6 knockdown lowers serum IL-6
safety.quote: the mice bearing Raji cells treated with ssCART-19 cells showed significant lower IL-6 levels in serum than those treated with regular CART-19 cells, but comparable anti-tumor efficacy between the animal groups.

safety.magnitude_basis: grade >=3 CRS 14.9% (ssCART-19) vs 37.5% (conventional CART-19), post hoc across two trials
safety.confidence_note: Open-access full text (PMC11456753) read; non-randomized post hoc comparison of two trials (NCT03275493 sponsor). Paper cites the preclinical IL-6 reduction as its rationale.
safety.judgement: Model predicted lower IL-6-driven CRS with the CRS-suppression CAR; patients had less grade >=3 CRS with comparable CR/CRi. Model published 2020 before the patient comparison (2024), so not a retrodiction.
safety.note: Patients on ssCART-19 had less severe CRS and ICANS than on conventional CD19 CAR T, as the mouse IL-6 data predicted.
safety.short: Less severe CRS in patients, as predicted
safety.quote: Grade ≥3 CRS occurred in 14.89% (7/47) of the ssCART-19 group versus 37.5% (15/40) in the cCART-19 group (p = 0.036).
safety.reason: Same: less severe CRS, as mouse IL-6 predicted

considered_not_added: Brexucabtagene product phenotype (CCR7+CD45RA+ naive T cells) as response correlate: published for ZUMA-2/ZUMA-7 (MCL, LBCL), no ALL (ZUMA-3) model-vs-patient comparison found; product characterization rather than a model system
TBI-1501 (Takara/Otsuka): only press releases and registry listing found; no published preclinical model compared with patients
BinD19: no preclinical or patient publication found
Norelli/Giavridis IL-1 blockade (anakinra) prediction: concerns a co-medication to mitigate toxicity, not one of this class's four questions
Rhesus macaque CAR T neurotoxicity model (Taraseviciute 2018): CD20 CAR, sibling target outside the class
In-silico CAR T cellular-kinetic models: published for tisagenlecleucel/axicabtagene, not member drugs
JCAR015 ROCKET cerebral-edema deaths (NCT02535364, 2016-17): patient outcome that belongs as a note on the draft's nalm6-scid-beige-19-28z safety track, not a new model system
Davila 2014 (19-28z adults): intermediate patient source on the draft's existing nalm6 track, no new system
